approved_findings: Both captures describe the same Stripe-hosted redirect flow under the exact URL (old 1, 4-6; new 1, 5-9): create a Checkout Session on the server, redirect to its URL, and collect payment on a prebuilt Stripe page. The new capture expands the scope to multiple backend and frontend code samples; it does not replace this URL with the separate embedded guide represented in source 8, 24-41, 84.

New prose explicitly recommends passing integration_identifier to compare conversion for implementations/segments (new 161-169), keeping sensitive price and availability on the server (new 171-173), and waiting for payment success before fulfilling after the return redirect (new 215-217, 1121-1123). The old guide mentioned a server endpoint and fulfillment event destination (old 21, 152), but did not give these two new security/finality qualifications. Current source 21 labels query-param display but should not let it imply payment proof.

Core older behavior remains: payment/subscription/setup modes (old 25-27; new 175-177), public success URL and session.url redirect (old 27, 60, 66; new 179-189), preview before redirect because the order is then final (old 76; new 191-209), test card scenarios (old 135-141; new 239-247), and Customer versus guest handling (old 143-148; new 288-298).

New customer_account language narrows the old blanket Accounts v2 shorthand: it applies when customers are represented as customer-configured Account objects, and an Account ID prefills the associated email (new 298; old 148; source 20, 57). It is a conditional identity route, not a universal replacement for customer IDs.

The new raw is a flattened aggregate of language/frontend variants: duplicate headings/prose and alternative local ports (new 159-169, 191-237), repeated YOUR_DOMAIN and success_url assignments and {{CHECKOUT_MODE}} placeholders in sample fragments (new 300-332), varied package versions (new 333-388, 641-681, 749-824). These do not constitute one runnable program or prove a changed Checkout API requirement; use prose for durable claims and treat examples as variant-specific.

New Checkout studio is described as a build/preview and Dashboard configuration/monitoring route without writing code first (new 11, 1141-1143). It is an optional route; no account eligibility, deployment, conversion, or payment result is established.
approved_conflicts: The current source's hosted client pattern is expressed as success/canceled URL-query checks (source 21), while new 217 expressly delays fulfillment until payment succeeds. Clarify that query parameters are UI messaging, not payment status or shipping authorization. Source 69 mentions checkout.session.completed but must not imply every completion is paid; payment-status and delayed-method details require the separate fulfillment authority.

The current source says Accounts v2 uses customer_account through the old raw 148, whereas new 298 makes that field conditional on customer-configured Account objects. Preserve v1 customer ID and v2 Account identity distinctly.
historical_claims_to_preserve: The old 2026-04-20 hosted Node/React example, its local proxy and URL-query display pattern remain dated sample choices (old 36-70, 78-127, 129-133); new 215-217 makes clear display/redirect is not order-fulfillment proof.

The existing summary also covers a separate embedded raw (source 8, 24-41, 84), which was not within this exact job. Preserve its evidence and avoid importing the new hosted raw as authority for embedded behavior.

Three Checkout modes, order-preview finality after redirect, test-card scenarios, and guest versus Customer choice remain supported in both captures (old 25-27, 76, 135-148; new 175-177, 193-209, 239-247, 288-298).
